Subscriptions should be in the `active` or `trialing` state to be migrated.

(For backwards compatibility reasons, it is possible to migrate a subscription that is in the `trial_ended` state via the API, however this is not recommended.  Since `trial_ended` is an end-of-life state, the subscription should be canceled, the product changed, and then the subscription can be reactivated.)

For more information, see [Product Changes and Migrations](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/management/subscription-actions/understand-upgrade-and-downgrade-scenarios).

Important note: One of the most common ways that a migration can fail is when the attempt is made to migrate a subscription to its current product.

put.description:
Reactivates a previously canceled subscription. For details on how the reactivation works, and how to reactivate subscriptions through the application, see [reactivation](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/management/state-management/understand-reactivation-and-resume-scenarios).

**Note: The term "resume" is used also during another process in Advanced Billing. This occurs when an on-hold subscription is "resumed". This returns the subscription to an active state.**

+ The response returns the subscription object in the `active` or `trialing` state.
+ The `canceled_at` and `cancellation_message` fields do not have values.
+ The method works for "Canceled" or "Trial Ended" subscriptions.
+ It will not work for items not marked as "Canceled", "Unpaid", or "Trial Ended".

## Resume the current billing period for a subscription

A subscription is considered "resumable" if you are attempting to reactivate within the billing period the subscription was canceled in.

A resumed subscription's billing date remains the same as before it was canceled. In other words, it does not start a new billing period. Payment may or may not be collected for a resumed subscription, depending on whether or not the subscription had a balance when it was canceled (for example, if it was canceled because of dunning).

Consider a subscription which was created on June 1st, and would renew on July 1st. The subscription is then canceled on June 15.

If a reactivation with `resume: true` were attempted _before_ what would have been the next billing date of July 1st, then Advanced Billing would resume the subscription.

If a reactivation with `resume: true` were attempted _after_ what would have been the next billing date of July 1st, then Advanced Billing would not resume the subscription, and instead it would be reactivated with a new billing period.

If a reactivation with `resume: false`, or where 'resume' is omitted were attempted, then Advanced Billing would reactivate the subscription with a new billing period regardless of whether or not resuming the previous billing period was possible.

| Canceled | Reactivation | Resumable? |
|---|---|---|
| Jun 15 | June 28 | Yes |
| Jun 15 | July 2 | No |

## Reactivation Scenarios

### Reactivating Canceled Subscription While Preserving Balance

+ Given you have a product that costs $20
+ Given you have a canceled subscription to the $20 product
    + 1 charge should exist for $20
    + 1 payment should exist for $20
+ When the subscription has canceled due to dunning, it retained a negative balance of $20

#### Results

The resulting charges upon reactivation will be:
+ 1 charge for $20 for the new product
+ 1 charge for $20 for the balance due
+ Total charges = $40

+ The subscription will transition to active
+ The subscription balance will be zero

### Reactivating a Canceled Subscription With Coupon

+ Given you have a canceled subscription
+ It has no current period defined
+ You have a coupon code "EARLYBIRD"
+ The coupon is set to recur for 6 periods

PUT request sent to:
`https://acme.chargify.com/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/reactivate.json?coupon_code=EARLYBIRD`

#### Results

+ The subscription will transition to active
+ The subscription should have applied a coupon with code "EARLYBIRD"

### Reactivating Canceled Subscription With a Trial, Without the include_trial Flag

+ Given you have a canceled subscription
+ The product associated with the subscription has a trial

+ PUT request to
`https://acme.chargify.com/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/reactivate.json`


#### Results
+ The subscription will transition to active

### Reactivating Canceled Subscription With Trial, With the include_trial Flag

+ Given you have a canceled subscription
+ The product associated with the subscription has a trial

+ Send a PUT request to `https://acme.chargify.com/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/reactivate.json?include_trial=1`


#### Results

+ The subscription will transition to trialing

### Reactivating Trial Ended Subscription

+ Given you have a trial_ended subscription
+ Send a PUT request to `https://acme.chargify.com/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/reactivate.json`

#### Results

+ The subscription will transition to active

### Resuming a Canceled Subscription

+ Given you have a `canceled` subscription and it is resumable
+ Send a PUT request to `https://acme.chargify.com/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/reactivate.json?resume=true`

#### Results

+ The subscription will transition to active
+ The next billing date should not have changed

### Attempting to resume a subscription which is not resumable

+ Given you have a `canceled` subscription, and it is not resumable
+ Send a PUT request to `https://acme.chargify.com/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/reactivate.json?resume=true`

#### Results

+ The subscription will transition to active, with a new billing period.

### Attempting to resume but not reactivate a subscription which is not resumable

+ Given you have a `canceled` subscription, and it is not resumable
+ Send a PUT request to `https://acme.chargify.com/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/reactivate.json?resume[require_resume]=true`
+ The response status should be "422 UNPROCESSABLE ENTITY"
+ The subscription should be canceled with the following response
```
  {
    "errors": ["Request was 'resume only', but this subscription cannot be resumed."]
  }
```

#### Results

+ The subscription should remain `canceled`
+ The next billing date should not have changed

### Resuming Subscription Which Was Trialing

+ Given you have a `trial_ended` subscription, and it is resumable
+ And the subscription was canceled in the middle of a trial
+ And there is still time left on the trial
+ Send a PUT request to `https://acme.chargify.com/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/reactivate.json?resume=true`

#### Results

+ The subscription will transition to trialing
+ The next billing date should not have changed

### Resuming Subscription Which Was trial_ended

+ Given you have a `trial_ended` subscription, and it is resumable
+ Send a PUT request to `https://acme.chargify.com/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/reactivate.json?resume=true`

#### Results

+ The subscription will transition to active
+ The next billing date should not have changed
+ Any product-related charges should have been collected

post.description:
Previews a subscription’s next renewal assessment. Renewal Preview is an object representing a subscription’s next assessment. You can retrieve it to see a snapshot of how much your customer will be charged on their next renewal.

The "Next Billing" amount and "Next Billing" date are already represented in the UI on each Subscriber's Summary. For more information, see [Subscriber Interface Overview](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/billing-portal/using/see-the-billing-portal-screens-subscribers-use).

## Optional Component Fields

This endpoint is particularly useful because it returns the computed billing amount for the base product and the components which are in use by a subscriber.

By default, the preview includes billing details for all components _at their **current** quantities_. This means:

* Current `allocated_quantity` for quantity-based components
* Current enabled/disabled status for on/off components
* Current metered usage `unit_balance` for metered components
* Current metric quantity value for events recorded thus far for events-based components

In the above statements, "current" means the quantity or value as of the call to the renewal preview endpoint. End-of-period values for components are not predicted, so metered or events-based usage may be less than it will eventually be at the end of the period.

Optionally, **you can provide your own custom quantities** for any component to see a billing preview for non-current quantities. This is accomplished by sending a request body with data under the `components` key. See the request body documentation below.

## Preview Behavior

Sending a `POST` request to this endpoint returns preview data without modifying the subscription. This method previews data, but does not log any changes against a subscription.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
A key you generate, such as a UUID, that makes retrying this request safe. 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters; surrounding double quotes are ignored. Keys are scoped to your site and kept for at least 24 hours.

The first request with a key runs normally. A retry with the same key, method, path and query string, and a byte-identical body returns the stored status and body of that first request without running it again. The same key with a different request returns `422` (`idempotency_key_mismatch`). A retry that arrives while the first request is still running waits for it to finish, and returns `409` (`idempotency_request_in_progress`) only if that wait times out; on Create Wallet Purchase the `409` is immediate. Only successful responses are stored, so a failed request can be retried with the same key. When this header is sent, `uniqueness_token` is not checked.

See [Idempotent retries](page:introduction/basic-concepts/wallets#idempotent-retries) for the details, including how wallet purchases differ.

post.description:
Grants units to the wallet, or debits units from it, depending on `kind`. `amount` is always sent positive, and `kind` determines the direction written to the ledger.

**`kind: grant`**: a one-time manual top-up. On a non-negative balance, this creates a grant and writes one ledger row. On a negative balance, it repays the overdraft first (a `kind: grant` row with `grant_id: null`, for the repaid amount), then creates the grant: its `original` is always the full `amount` sent, and its `remaining` is what's left after the overdraft was repaid, which is `0` if the overdraft absorbed the whole top-up. The grant row is still written, and its `amount` is that `remaining`, not `original`, so the ledger rows sum to the balance change. A grant may carry `expires_at`; a debit may not.

**`kind: debit`**: direct consumption. Drains grants earliest-expiration-first, one `kind: debit` row per grant touched, plus any overdue expiration rows this same call triggers first (see below):
- Under the wallet's default `hard_stop_overflow: discard`, the drain is capped at the available balance. For a metered wallet, that cap is the live metered balance, not the stored one, so a debit can drain less than its stored balance would suggest, or even drain nothing at all (`201` with `drained_amount: "0.0"`) if live usage has already consumed what the ledger hadn't caught up to yet. A debit against a wallet whose *stored* balance is already zero or negative (`discard` only ever reaches zero) returns `422 "Wallet is depleted"`. Before that failure is returned, this call still expires any grants that were already overdue, so a `422` response can still leave new `kind: expiration` rows written.
- Under `hard_stop_overflow: allow_negative`, the full amount is deducted. The excess past the wallet's grants is booked as one overdraft row with `grant_id: null`, `rejected_amount` is always `"0.0"`, and the balance goes negative.

post.description:
Posts a signed correction against a specific grant (or, for an overdraft entry, against the overdraft): positive adds units to the grant, negative removes them. `reason` is required and is written to the ledger row's `memo`. Writes exactly one ledger row, of kind `adjustment`.

Use `source_transaction_id` to name a specific `debit` row when you're correcting one recorded consumption rather than the grant's balance as a whole. When it names a grant-attributed debit, it's recorded for audit only: naming it doesn't change how `amount` is applied, and more than one adjustment may name the same row. When it names an overdraft entry, it switches the correction to the overdraft path described below.

An overdraft entry (a `debit` row with no `grant_id`, written when an `allow_negative` wallet consumes past its grants) can be corrected without a `grant_id`. That correction is credit-only, credits no grant, and is bounded by the usage the entry still records and by the overdraft the wallet still owes. Once a later grant has repaid the overdraft, correct that grant's balance instead.

An adjustment corrects the ledger, so it works on the grant's recorded remainder, `posted_remaining`, not on `remaining`, which on a metered wallet read through [Read Wallet]($e/Wallets/readWallet) also subtracts usage not yet posted. Send `posted_remaining` back as `expected_remaining`; sending `remaining` on a metered wallet with pending usage returns `409`.

`expected_remaining` and `expected_source_corrections` are optional optimistic-concurrency checks; see their field descriptions. Use them when the correction's `amount` was derived from a value read earlier that might have moved since.

post.description:
Purchases prepaid units for the wallet and charges the subscription's payment method for them, using the wallet's `price_point_id` unless a different price point is named. A successful purchase writes a grant of origin `purchase`, with its expiration following the funding entitlement's grant expiration policy.

How "charged" works depends on the subscription's collection method. For card/automatic collection, the payment is attempted immediately; a decline writes nothing to the wallet, and the call fails with a `422` naming the gateway's decline reason. For invoice-billed (remittance) subscriptions, there's no immediate charge to decline: an invoice is drafted, the wallet is credited right away, and the invoice is issued afterward. If issuing the invoice fails at that point, the invoice is left in draft state and reported for follow-up, but the call still returns `201` and the units already credited are **not** rolled back. See [Preview Wallet Purchase]($e/Wallet%20Purchases/previewWalletPurchase) to quote a price before charging anything.

revert_on_failure.description: You may choose how to handle the activation failure. `true` means do not change the subscription’s state and billing period. `false` means to continue through with the activation and enter an end-of-life state. If this parameter is omitted or `null` is passed it will default to the value set in the site settings (default: `true`).

total.description: Total count of active wallets drawing on this product.

sample.description: Up to 50 of the most recently created active wallets, newest first.

amount.description: Signed: positive adds units to the grant, negative removes them. Bounded below by the grant's `posted_remaining` (a correction can't drive it negative) and above by the grant's `original` (a correction can't credit past what was originally granted). An out-of-bounds value is rejected rather than clamped. Zero is rejected. Without a `grant_id` (an overdraft correction), the amount must be positive, can't exceed the usage the overdraft entry still records, and can't exceed the overdraft the wallet still owes. Encoded as a decimal string with at most 8 fractional digits. Send fractional values as strings: a JSON number with a decimal point is rejected with `422`, because a double-precision float may already have lost precision before the request arrives.

reason.description: Required. Lands on the resulting ledger row's `memo`.

grant_id.description: The grant to correct. Must belong to this wallet. Required unless `source_transaction_id` names an overdraft entry (a `debit` with no `grant_id`, written when an `allow_negative` wallet consumes past its grants). For an overdraft entry, omit it: sending one returns `422`, and the correction credits the wallet's outstanding overdraft instead of any grant.

source_transaction_id.description: (Optional) The `debit` row this correction is fixing. Must belong to this wallet, and must name a row of kind `debit`; grant and adjustment rows are append-only history, corrected by posting a further adjustment rather than by pointing at them. For a grant-attributed debit, it's recorded on the resulting ledger row for audit only: it does not change how `amount` is applied, and more than one adjustment may name the same row. For an overdraft entry, it decides the path: omit `grant_id`, and the correction is credit-only, bounded by the usage the entry still records and by the overdraft the wallet still owes.

expected_remaining.description: (Optional) An optimistic-concurrency check for a caller whose `amount` was derived from the grant's own remainder. Send the grant's `posted_remaining`, not its `remaining`: on a metered wallet read through [Read Wallet]($e/Wallets/readWallet), `remaining` also subtracts usage not yet posted, so it can differ from what the adjustment checks. If given and the grant's current `posted_remaining` no longer matches, the request is rejected with `409` and nothing is written. Compared numerically, so `"100"` and `"100.00000000"` both match a `posted_remaining` of `100`. Omit the field entirely to skip the check; sending it as an empty string is treated as a malformed value (`422`), not as an omission.

expected_source_corrections.description: (Optional) An optimistic-concurrency check for a caller whose `amount` was derived from a usage entry, sent together with `source_transaction_id`: the entry's `source_corrections_total` as the caller last read it (`"0"` if none). If the sum the server computes no longer matches, the request is rejected with `409` and nothing is written. This is what catches a correction posted between that read and this request. Ignored unless `source_transaction_id` is also given.

AggregatedEntitlement.title: AggregatedEntitlement

feature_key.description: The feature's key, prefixed by kind: `feature.*` for `access_right`, `usage.*` for `usage_limit`, `service.*` for `service_right`.

periodicity_key.description: Uniquely identifies this aggregated entry: the prefixed feature key, suffixed with `:{interval}:{unit}` when the entitlement has a periodicity window. Equal to `feature_key` when `periodicity` is `null`.

allOf.description:
The behavior of a feature:
- `access_right`: a boolean entitlement. A subscriber either has access or does not.
- `usage_limit`: a quantified allowance measured over a recurring period (for example, "10,000 API calls per month").
- `service_right`: a free-form value (text, boolean, or number) that isn't a simple access flag or a metered limit.

value.description: The aggregated value, coerced according to `type`: a boolean for `access_right` (and boolean `service_right`), a number for `usage_limit` (and numeric `service_right`), or a string for text `service_right`.

enabled.description: `true` only when the aggregated value is truthy for this feature's kind, and the subscription is in a live state (`active`, `trialing`, `assessing`, `past_due`, or `soft_failure`). `false` otherwise, including for `awaiting_signup`, canceled, expired, and on-hold subscriptions. Entitlements deliberately stay enabled through dunning.

source_products.description: The names of the products/components contributing to this entitlement. For `access_right` features, only contributors that granted `true` are listed.

AggregatedEntitlement.description: One entitlement in a subscriber's aggregated entitlements list. Entries are aggregated per feature key and periodicity window, not per feature key alone. A `usage_limit` feature granted with two different periodicities yields two entries sharing one `feature_key`. Use `periodicity_key` to identify an entry uniquely.

allOf.description: The recurring window over which a `usage_limit` feature's allowance resets.

CloneFeatureCatalogItem.description:
A feature to put on the cloned price point. Requires Entitlements to be enabled for the site; ignored otherwise.

Unlike Create Feature Catalog Item, nothing falls back to the feature template's defaults: send `value`, and for a `usage_limit` feature its periodicity (and any grant expiration) explicitly. If any item can't be applied, for example a missing `value`, a `usage_limit` item without periodicity, or an archived or unknown feature template, the whole clone fails with `422` and nothing is created.

allOf.description:
The kind of tax or business identifier held by the customer:
- `vat_eu`: an EU VAT number. Requires `vat_country` to be an EU member state code or `GB`.
- `national_tax`: a national tax ID registered outside the EU. Requires `vat_country` to be one of `AL`, `AM`, `AR`, `AU`, `BR`, `CA`, `CH`, `DZ`, `IN`, `MX`, `NO`, `NZ`, or `ZA`.
- `company_reg`: a company registration number, such as a French SIREN. No `vat_country` is required.
- `gln`: a Global Location Number. The value must be 13 digits.
- `duns`: a D-U-N-S Number. The value must be 9 digits.
- `lei`: a Legal Entity Identifier. The value must be 20 characters: 18 letters or digits followed by 2 digits.

A customer holds one identifier at a time. Saving an identifier of a different kind replaces the existing one.

branding_theme_id.description: The ID of the Branding Theme to assign to this subscription. When set, this subscription-level Branding Theme is used instead of the customer's default Branding Theme for subscription-related documents and communications that use subscription theming. Pass null or an empty value to clear the subscription-level Branding Theme. Available only when Branding Themes are enabled for the site. Not returned in the response.

next_billing_at.description: (Optional) Set this attribute to a future date/time to sync imported subscriptions to your existing renewal schedule. See the notes on “Date/Time Format” in our [subscription import documentation](https://docs.maxio.com/configuration/importing/import-subscriptions-from-a-csv#date-format). If you provide a next_billing_at timestamp that is in the future, no trial or initial charges will be applied when you create the subscription. In fact, no payment will be captured at all. The first payment will be captured, according to the prices defined by the product, near the time specified by next_billing_at. If you do not provide a value for next_billing_at, any trial and/or initial charges will be assessed and charged at the time of subscription creation. If the card cannot be successfully charged, the subscription will not be created. See further notes in the section on Importing Subscriptions.

initial_billing_at.description: (Optional) Set this attribute to a future date/time to create a subscription in the Awaiting Signup state, rather than Active or Trialing. You can omit the initial_billing_at date to activate the subscription immediately. In the Awaiting Signup state, a subscription behaves like any other. It can be canceled, allocated to, or have its billing date changed. etc. When the initial_billing_at date hits, the subscription will transition to the expected state. If the product has a trial, the subscription will enter a trial, otherwise it will go active. Setup fees will be respected either before or after the trial, as configured on the price point. If the payment is due at the initial_billing_at and it fails the subscription will be immediately canceled. See the [subscription import](https://docs.maxio.com/configuration/importing/import-subscriptions-from-a-csv#date-format) documentation for more information about Date/Time Formats.

defer_signup.description: (Optional) Set this attribute to true to create the subscription in the Awaiting Signup Date state. Use this when you want to create a subscription that has an unknown first billing date. When the first billing date is known, update a subscription and set the `initial_billing_at` date. The subscription moves to the Awaiting Signup state with a scheduled initial billing date. You can omit the initial_billing_at date to activate the subscription immediately. See [Subscription States](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/management/subscription-states/understand-subscription-states#setup-and-transient-states) for more information.

stored_credential_transaction_id.description: For European sites subject to PSD2 and using 3D Secure, this can be used to reference a previous transaction for the customer. This will ensure the card will be charged successfully at renewal.

payment_profile_id.description: The Payment Profile ID of an existing card or bank account, which belongs to an existing customer to use for payment for this subscription. If the card, bank account, or customer does not exist already, or if you want to use a new (unstored) card or bank account for the subscription, use `payment_profile_attributes` instead to create a new payment profile along with the subscription. (This value is available on an existing subscription via the API as `credit_card` > id or `bank_account` > id.)

ref.description: A valid referral code. (optional, see [Referrals](https://docs.maxio.com/configuration/advanced-billing/understand-referrals#find-a-referral-code) for more details). If supplied, must be valid, or else subscription creation will fail.

cancellation_message.description: (Optional) Can be used when canceling a subscription (via the HTTP DELETE method) to make a note about the reason for cancellation.

cancellation_method.description: (Optional) Can be used when canceling a subscription (via the HTTP DELETE method) to make a note about how the subscription was canceled.

currency.description: (Optional) If Multi-Currency is enabled and the currency is configured in Chargify, pass it at signup to create a subscription on a non-default currency. Note that you cannot update the currency of an existing subscription.

expiration_tracks_next_billing_change.description: (Optional, default false) When set to true, and when next_billing_at is present, if the subscription expires, the expires_at will be shifted by the same amount of time as the difference between the old and new “next billing” dates.

agreement_terms.description: (Optional) The ACH authorization agreement terms. If enabled, an email will be sent to the customer with a copy of the terms.

authorizer_first_name.description: (Optional) The first name of the person authorizing the ACH agreement.

authorizer_last_name.description: (Optional) The last name of the person authorizing the ACH agreement.

calendar_billing_first_charge.description: (Optional) One of “prorated” (the default – the prorated product price will be charged immediately), “immediate” (the full product price will be charged immediately), or “delayed” (the full product price will be charged with the first scheduled renewal).

reason_code.description: (Optional) Can be used when canceling a subscription (via the HTTP DELETE method) to indicate why a subscription was canceled.

product_change_delayed.description: (Optional) used only for Delayed Product Change When set to true, indicates that a changed value for product_handle should schedule the product change to the next subscription renewal.

offer_id.description: Use in place of passing product and component information to set up the subscription with an existing offer. May be either the Chargify id of the offer or its handle prefixed with `handle:`.

previous_billing_at.description: Providing a previous_billing_at that is in the past will set the current_period_starts_at when the subscription is created. It will also set activated_at if not explicitly passed during the subscription import. Can only be used if next_billing_at is also passed. Using this option will allow you to set the period start for the subscription so mid period component allocations have the correct prorated amount.

import_mrr.description: Setting this attribute to true will cause the subscription's MRR to be added to your MRR analytics immediately. For this value to be honored, a next_billing_at must be present and set to a future date. This key/value will not be returned in the subscription response body.

(Optional) If passed, the proof of the authorized ACH agreement terms will be persisted.

dunning_communication_delay_enabled.description: Enable Communication Delay feature, making sure no communication (email or SMS) is sent to the Customer between 9PM and 8AM in time zone set by the `dunning_communication_delay_time_zone` attribute.

skip_billing_manifest_taxes.description: Valid only for the Subscription Preview endpoint. When set to `true` it skips calculating taxes for the current and next billing manifests. Defaults to `false` when not provided.

unit_balance.description: Used for metered and events based components.

allOf.description:
Create or update custom pricing unique to the subscription, used in place of `price_point_id`. Accepts every attribute of a component custom price, plus `segments` for setting per-segment rates on an event-based component.

Segment-level custom pricing requires a site on Maxio Metering and an event-based component whose meter has segmenting properties. The override takes effect as soon as the request succeeds and prices all of the current billing period's usage at the new rates, including usage recorded before the request. There is no option to schedule the change for a later date.

To read the segment rates back, take the `price_point_id` of the subscription's component (for example, from [Read Subscription Component]($e/Subscription%20Components/readSubscriptionComponent)) and call `GET /components/{component_id}/price_points/{price_point_id}/segments.json`.

uid.description: Unique identifier for the credit note. It is generated automatically by Chargify and has the prefix "cn_" followed by alphanumeric characters.

site_id.description: ID of the site to which the credit note belongs.

customer_id.description: ID of the customer to which the credit note belongs.

subscription_id.description: ID of the subscription that generated the credit note.

number.description:
A unique, identifying string that appears on the credit note and in places it is referenced.

While the UID is long and not appropriate to show to customers, the number is usually shorter and consumable by the customer and the merchant alike.

sequence_number.description: A monotonically increasing number assigned to credit notes as they are created.  This number is unique within a site and can be used to sort and order credit notes.

issue_date.description:
Date the credit note was issued to the customer.  This is the date that the credit was made available for application, and may come before it is fully applied.

The format is `"YYYY-MM-DD"`.

applied_date.description:
Credit notes are applied to invoices to offset invoiced amounts - they reduce the amount due. This field is the date the credit note became fully applied to invoices.

If the credit note has been partially applied, this field will not have a value until it has been fully applied.

The format is `"YYYY-MM-DD"`.

allOf.description: Current status of the credit note.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 currency code (3 character string) representing the currency of the credit note amount fields.

memo.description: The memo printed on credit note, which is a description of the reason for the credit.

allOf.description: Information about the seller (merchant) listed on the masthead of the credit note.
Information about the customer who is owner or recipient of the credited subscription.
The billing address of the credit subscription.
The shipping address of the credited subscription.

subtotal_amount.description: Subtotal of the credit note, which is the sum of all line items before discounts or taxes. Note that this is a positive amount representing the credit back to the customer.

discount_amount.description: Total discount applied to the credit note. Note that this is a positive amount representing the discount amount being credited back to the customer (i.e., a credit on an earlier discount). For example, if the original purchase was $1.00 and the original discount was $0.10, a credit of $0.50 of the original purchase (half) would have a discount credit of $0.05 (also half).

tax_amount.description: Total tax of the credit note. Note that this is a positive amount representing a previously taxed amount being credited back to the customer (i.e., a credit of an earlier tax). For example, if the original purchase was $1.00 and the original tax was $0.10, a credit of $0.50 of the original purchase (half) would also have a tax credit of $0.05 (also half).

total_amount.description: The credit note total, which is `subtotal_amount - discount_amount + tax_amount`.

applied_amount.description: The amount of the credit note that has already been applied to invoices.

remaining_amount.description: The amount of the credit note remaining to be applied to invoices, which is `total_amount - applied_amount`.

line_items.description: Line items on the credit note.

origin_invoices.description: An array of origin invoices for the credit note. Learn more about [Origin Invoice from our docs](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/invoicing/working-with-invoices/how-credit-notes-work#how-origin-invoices-work).

uid.description: Unique identifier for the line item.  Useful when cross-referencing the line against individual discounts in the `discounts` or `taxes` lists.

title.description: A short descriptor for the credit given by this line.

description.description:
Detailed description for the credit given by this line.  May include proration details in plain text.

Note: this string may contain line breaks that are hints for the best display format on the credit note.

quantity.description:
The quantity or count of units credited by the line item.

This is a decimal number represented as a string. (See "About Decimal Numbers".)

unit_price.description:
The price per unit for the line item.

When tiered pricing was used (i.e., not every unit was actually priced at the same price) this will be the blended average cost per unit and the `tiered_unit_price` field will be set to `true`.

subtotal_amount.description: The line subtotal, generally calculated as `quantity * unit_price`. This is the canonical amount of record for the line - when rounding differences are in play, `subtotal_amount` takes precedence over the value derived from `quantity * unit_price` (which may not have the proper precision to exactly equal this amount).

discount_amount.description:
The approximate discount of just this line.

The value is approximated in cases where rounding errors make it difficult to apportion exactly a total discount among many lines. Several lines may have been summed prior to applying the discount to arrive at `discount_amount` for the invoice - backing that out to the discount on a single line may introduce rounding or precision errors.

tax_amount.description:
The approximate tax of just this line.

The value is approximated in cases where rounding errors make it difficult to apportion exactly a total tax among many lines. Several lines may have been summed prior to applying the tax rate to arrive at `tax_amount` for the invoice - backing that out to the tax on a single line may introduce rounding or precision errors.

tax_included.description:
Whether the unit price for this line item is tax-inclusive.

When `true`, `unit_price` already includes tax and `tax_amount` represents the portion of the price attributable to tax. When `false`, any applicable tax is added on top of the price.

The value is inherited from the source price point's `tax_included` setting. Custom or ad-hoc line items (which have no associated price point) always return `false`.

total_amount.description:
The non-canonical total amount for the line.

`subtotal_amount` is the canonical amount for a line. The invoice `total_amount` is derived from the sum of the line `subtotal_amount`s and discounts or taxes applied thereafter.  Therefore, due to rounding or precision errors, the sum of line `total_amount`s may not equal the invoice `total_amount`.

tiered_unit_price.description: When `true`, indicates that the actual pricing scheme for the line was tiered, so the `unit_price` shown is the blended average for all units.

period_range_start.description: Start date for the period credited by this line. The format is `"YYYY-MM-DD"`.

period_range_end.description: End date for the period credited by this line. The format is `"YYYY-MM-DD"`.

product_id.description:
The ID of the product being credited.

This may be set even for component credits, so true product-only (non-component) credits will also have a nil `component_id`.

product_version.description: The version of the product being credited.

component_id.description: The ID of the component being credited. Will be `nil` for non-component credits.

price_point_id.description: The price point ID of the component being credited. Will be `nil` for non-component credits.

prepaid_allocation_expires_at.description: The date a prepaid allocation is set to expire. Only present on line items representing prepaid component allocations. The format is `"YYYY-MM-DD"`.

allOf.description:
Price point type. We expose the following types:
1. **default**: a price point that is marked as a default price for a certain product.
2. **custom**: a custom price point.
3. **catalog**: a price point that is **not** marked as a default price for a certain product and is **not** a custom one.

default.description: Note: Refer to type attribute instead.

allOf.description: The identifier for the pricing scheme. See [Product Components](https://help.chargify.com/products/product-components.html) for an overview of pricing schemes.

use_site_exchange_rate.description: Whether to use the site level exchange rate or define your own prices for each currency if you have multiple currencies defined on the site. Defaults to true during creation.

subscription_id.description: (only used for Custom Pricing - ie. when the price point's type is `custom`) The id of the subscription that the custom price point is for.

interval.description: The numerical interval. e.g., an interval of ‘30’ coupled with an interval_unit of day would mean this component price point would renew every 30 days. This property is only available for sites with Multifrequency enabled.

allOf.description: A string representing the interval unit for this component price point, either month or day. This property is only available for sites with Multifrequency enabled.

currency_prices.description: An array of currency pricing data is available when multiple currencies are defined for the site. It varies based on the use_site_exchange_rate setting for the price point. This parameter is present only in the response of read endpoints, after including the appropriate query parameter. The clone endpoint always returns currency prices if they are present.

overage_prices.description: Applicable only to prepaid usage components. An array of overage price brackets.

allOf.description: Applicable only to prepaid usage components. Pricing scheme for overage pricing.

secondary_prices.description: Returned only for hybrid price points. An array of secondary price brackets. Hybrid price points never return `overage_prices` or `overage_pricing_scheme`.

allOf.description: Returned only for hybrid price points. Pricing scheme for the secondary pricing model.

renew_prepaid_allocation.description: Applicable only to prepaid usage components. Boolean which controls whether or not the allocated quantity should be renewed at the beginning of each period.

rollover_prepaid_remainder.description: Applicable only to prepaid usage components. Boolean which controls whether or not remaining units should be rolled over to the next period.

expiration_interval.description: Applicable only to prepaid usage components where rollover_prepaid_remainder is true. The number of `expiration_interval_unit`s after which rollover amounts should expire.

allOf.description: Applicable only to prepaid usage components where rollover_prepaid_remainder is true. A string representing the expiration interval unit for this component, either month or day.

currency_overage_prices.description: Applicable only to prepaid usage components. An array of currency pricing data for overage prices.

currency_secondary_prices.description: Returned only for hybrid price points, by List All Component Price Points with `include=currency_secondary_prices` or `include=currency_overage_prices`. An array of currency pricing data for secondary prices.

EntityIdentifierKind.title: EntityIdentifierKind
EntityIdentifierKind.description:
The kind of tax or business identifier held by the customer:
- `vat_eu`: an EU VAT number. Requires `vat_country` to be an EU member state code or `GB`.
- `national_tax`: a national tax ID registered outside the EU. Requires `vat_country` to be one of `AL`, `AM`, `AR`, `AU`, `BR`, `CA`, `CH`, `DZ`, `IN`, `MX`, `NO`, `NZ`, or `ZA`.
- `company_reg`: a company registration number, such as a French SIREN. No `vat_country` is required.
- `gln`: a Global Location Number. The value must be 13 digits.
- `duns`: a D-U-N-S Number. The value must be 9 digits.
- `lei`: a Legal Entity Identifier. The value must be 20 characters: 18 letters or digits followed by 2 digits.

A customer holds one identifier at a time. Saving an identifier of a different kind replaces the existing one.

* The rest, that is `delayed_signup_creation_failure`, `billing_date_change`, `expiration_date_change`, `expiring_card`, 
`customer_update`, `customer_create`, `customer_delete`, `upgrade_downgrade_success`, `upgrade_downgrade_failure`, 
`statement_closed`, `statement_settled`, `subscription_card_update`, `subscription_group_card_update`, 
`subscription_bank_account_update`, `refund_failure`, `upcoming_renewal_notice`, `trial_end_notice`,

`subscription_customer_change`, `account_transaction_changed`, `go_cardless_payment_paid_out`, `go_cardless_payment_rejected`,

FailedPaymentAction.title: FailedPaymentAction
FailedPaymentAction.description:
Action taken when payment for an invoice fails:
- `leave_open_invoice` - prepayments and credits applied to invoice; invoice status set to "open"; email sent to the customer for the issued invoice (if setting applies); payment failure recorded in the invoice history. This is the default option.
- `rollback_to_pending` - prepayments and credits not applied; invoice remains in "pending" status; no email sent to the customer; payment failure recorded in the invoice history.
- `initiate_dunning` - prepayments and credits applied to the invoice; invoice status set to "open"; email sent to the customer for the issued invoice (if setting applies); payment failure recorded in the invoice history; subscription will most likely go into "past_due" or "canceled" state (depending upon net terms and dunning settings).

Omit both to create a product/component-level item, which is a template: it is copied onto price points created afterwards (except bulk-created ones; Clone Component Price Point applies only the items sent with it), but not added to price points that already exist or to their subscribers.

propagate_to_subscriptions.description: Applies to price-point-scoped items only. When `true`, existing subscriptions on that price point are granted an entitlement for this feature by a background job shortly after, instead of at their next subscription change. When `false` (default) and the price point already has subscribers, the feature is created on a clone of the price point instead, and existing subscribers are unaffected. On a product/component-level item it has no effect, except when the call restores that item's archived price-point copies (creating an item again for a feature template whose item was archived): then `true` grants the feature to those price points' subscribers, and without it the call returns `422` if any of them lack the feature.

When `true`, existing subscriptions on the item's price point are updated with the new `value`/periodicity by a background job shortly after. Has no effect on a product/component-level item. When `false` (default) and the item's price point already has subscribers, the update is made on a clone of the price point instead, and existing subscribers are unaffected.

allOf.description:
The state of a subscription.
* **Live States**
    * `active` - A normal, active subscription. It is not in a trial and is paid and up to date.
    * `assessing` - An internal (transient) state that indicates a subscription is in the middle of periodic assessment. Do not base any access decisions in your app on this state, as it may not always be exposed.
    * `pending` - An internal (transient) state that indicates a subscription is in the creation process. Do not base any access decisions in your app on this state, as it may not always be exposed.
    * `trialing` - A subscription in trialing state has a valid trial subscription. This type of subscription may transition to active once payment is received when the trial has ended. Otherwise, it may go to a Problem or End of Life state.
    * `paused` - An internal state that indicates that your account with Advanced Billing is in arrears.
* **Problem States**
    * `past_due` - Indicates that the most recent payment has failed, and payment is past due for this subscription. If you have enabled our automated dunning, this subscription will be in the dunning process (additional status and callbacks from the dunning process will be available in the future). If you are handling dunning and payment updates yourself, you will want to use this state to initiate a payment update from your customers.
    * `soft_failure` - Indicates that normal assessment/processing of the subscription has failed for a reason that cannot be fixed by the Customer. For example, a Soft Fail may result from a timeout at the gateway or incorrect credentials on your part. The subscriptions should be retried automatically. An interface is being built for you to review problems resulting from these events to take manual action when needed.
    * `unpaid` - Indicates an unpaid subscription. A subscription is marked unpaid if the retry period expires and you have configured your [Dunning](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/dunning/overview/understanding-how-dunning-works) settings to have a Final Action of `mark the subscription unpaid`.
* **End of Life States**
    * `canceled` - Indicates a canceled subscription. This may happen at your request (via the API or the web interface) or due to the expiration of the [Dunning](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/dunning/overview/understanding-how-dunning-works) process without payment. See the [Reactivation](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/management/state-management/understand-reactivation-and-resume-scenarios) documentation for info on how to restart a canceled subscription.
    While a subscription is canceled, its period will not advance, it will not accrue any new charges, and Advanced Billing will not attempt to collect the overdue balance.
    * `expired` - Indicates a subscription that has expired due to running its normal life cycle. Some products may be configured to have an expiration period. An expired subscription then is one that stayed active until it fulfilled its full period.
    * `failed_to_create` - Indicates that signup has failed. (You may see this state in a signup_failure webhook.)
    * `on_hold` - Indicates that a subscription’s billing has been temporarily stopped. While it is expected that the subscription will resume and return to active status, this is still treated as an “End of Life” state because the customer is not paying for services during this time.
    * `suspended` - Indicates that a prepaid subscription has used up all their prepayment balance. If a prepayment is applied, it will return to an active state.
    * `trial_ended` - A subscription in a trial_ended state is a subscription that completed a no-obligation trial and did not have a card on file at the expiration of the trial period. See [Product Pricing – No Obligation Trials](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/plans/creating-plans) for more details.

See [Subscription States](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/management/subscription-states/understand-subscription-states) for more info about subscription states and state transitions.

InvoiceConsolidationLevel.title: InvoiceConsolidationLevel
InvoiceConsolidationLevel.description:
Consolidation level of the invoice, which is applicable to invoice consolidation. It will hold one of the following values:

* "none": A normal invoice with no consolidation.
* "child": An invoice segment which has been combined into a consolidated invoice.
* "parent": A consolidated invoice, whose contents are composed of invoice segments.

"Parent" invoices do not have lines of their own, but they have subtotals and totals which aggregate the member invoice segments.

See also the [invoice consolidation documentation](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/invoicing/working-with-invoices/understand-invoice-consolidation).

uid.description: Unique identifier for the line item. Useful when cross-referencing the line against individual discounts in the `discounts` or `taxes` lists.

title.description: A short descriptor for the charge or item represented by this line.

description.description:
Detailed description for the charge or item represented by this line. May include proration details in plain text.

Note: this string may contain line breaks that are hints for the best display format on the invoice.

quantity.description:
The quantity or count of units billed by the line item.

This is a decimal number represented as a string. (See "About Decimal Numbers".)

unit_price.description:
The price per unit for the line item.

When tiered pricing was used (i.e., not every unit was actually priced at the same price) this will be the blended average cost per unit and the `tiered_unit_price` field will be set to `true`.

subtotal_amount.description: The line subtotal, generally calculated as `quantity * unit_price`. This is the canonical amount of record for the line - when rounding differences are in play, `subtotal_amount` takes precedence over the value derived from `quantity * unit_price` (which may not have the proper precision to exactly equal this amount).

discount_amount.description:
The approximate discount applied to just this line.

The value is approximated in cases where rounding errors make it difficult to apportion exactly a total discount among many lines. Several lines may have been summed prior to applying the discount to arrive at `discount_amount` for the invoice - backing that out to the discount on a single line may introduce rounding or precision errors.

tax_amount.description:
The approximate tax applied to just this line.

The value is approximated in cases where rounding errors make it difficult to apportion exactly a total tax among many lines. Several lines may have been summed prior to applying the tax rate to arrive at `tax_amount` for the invoice - backing that out to the tax on a single line may introduce rounding or precision errors.

tax_included.description:
Whether the unit price for this line item is tax-inclusive.

When `true`, `unit_price` already includes tax and `tax_amount` represents the portion of the price attributable to tax. When `false`, any applicable tax is added on top of the price.

The value is inherited from the source price point's `tax_included` setting. Custom or ad-hoc line items (which have no associated price point) always return `false`.

total_amount.description:
The non-canonical total amount for the line.

`subtotal_amount` is the canonical amount for a line. The invoice `total_amount` is derived from the sum of the line `subtotal_amount`s and discounts or taxes applied thereafter. Therefore, due to rounding or precision errors, the sum of line `total_amount`s may not equal the invoice `total_amount`.

tiered_unit_price.description: When `true`, indicates that the actual pricing scheme for the line was tiered, so the `unit_price` shown is the blended average for all units.

period_range_start.description:
Start date for the period covered by this line. The format is `"YYYY-MM-DD"`.

* For periodic charges paid in advance, this date will match the billing date, and the end date will be in the future.
* For periodic charges paid in arrears (e.g., metered charges), this date will be the date of the previous billing, and the end date will be the current billing date.
* For non-periodic charges, this date and the end date will match.

period_range_end.description:
End date for the period covered by this line. The format is `"YYYY-MM-DD"`.

* For periodic charges paid in advance, this date will match the next (future) billing date.
* For periodic charges paid in arrears (e.g., metered charges), this date will be the date of the current billing date.
* For non-periodic charges, this date and the start date will match.

This may be set even for component charges, so true product-only (non-component) charges will also have a nil `component_id`.

allOf.description:
Action taken when payment for an invoice fails:
- `leave_open_invoice` - prepayments and credits applied to invoice; invoice status set to "open"; email sent to the customer for the issued invoice (if setting applies); payment failure recorded in the invoice history. This is the default option.
- `rollback_to_pending` - prepayments and credits not applied; invoice remains in "pending" status; no email sent to the customer; payment failure recorded in the invoice history.
- `initiate_dunning` - prepayments and credits applied to the invoice; invoice status set to "open"; email sent to the customer for the issued invoice (if setting applies); payment failure recorded in the invoice history; subscription will most likely go into "past_due" or "canceled" state (depending upon net terms and dunning settings).

Reason.title: Reason
Reason.description: Set whenever `status` isn't `active`. Accompanying `stopped`: `entitlement_missing` (an ordinary product or component change removed the entitlement), `wallet_archived` (the wallet was archived), `subscription_terminated` (the subscription reached a terminal state; funding resumes if the subscription returns to a granting state, for example on reactivation, without back-granting the periods it missed), `feature_removed` (the subscription no longer has this Feature), `wallet_behavior_disabled` (the Feature no longer has `wallet_behavior` configured), `superseded_by_replacement` (a later entitlement now funds this wallet instead), or `subscription_prepaid` (the subscription switched to prepaid, which cannot carry an active wallet). Accompanying `erroring`: `allowance_not_representable` (the entitlement's current allowance doesn't fit the wallet's amount encoding) or `balance_at_capacity` (granting it would push the balance past the maximum supported value).

    * `pending` - An internal (transient) state that indicates a subscription is in the creation process. Do not base any access decisions in your app on this state, as it may not always be exposed.
    * `trialing` - A subscription in trialing state has a valid trial subscription. This type of subscription may transition to active once payment is received when the trial has ended. Otherwise, it may go to a Problem or End of Life state.
    * `paused` - An internal state that indicates that your account with Advanced Billing is in arrears.
* **Problem States**
    * `past_due` - Indicates that the most recent payment has failed, and payment is past due for this subscription. If you have enabled our automated dunning, this subscription will be in the dunning process (additional status and callbacks from the dunning process will be available in the future). If you are handling dunning and payment updates yourself, you will want to use this state to initiate a payment update from your customers.
    * `soft_failure` - Indicates that normal assessment/processing of the subscription has failed for a reason that cannot be fixed by the Customer. For example, a Soft Fail may result from a timeout at the gateway or incorrect credentials on your part. The subscriptions should be retried automatically. An interface is being built for you to review problems resulting from these events to take manual action when needed.
    * `unpaid` - Indicates an unpaid subscription. A subscription is marked unpaid if the retry period expires and you have configured your [Dunning](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/dunning/overview/understanding-how-dunning-works) settings to have a Final Action of `mark the subscription unpaid`.
* **End of Life States**
    * `canceled` - Indicates a canceled subscription. This may happen at your request (via the API or the web interface) or due to the expiration of the [Dunning](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/dunning/overview/understanding-how-dunning-works) process without payment. See the [Reactivation](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/management/state-management/understand-reactivation-and-resume-scenarios) documentation for info on how to restart a canceled subscription.
    While a subscription is canceled, its period will not advance, it will not accrue any new charges, and Advanced Billing will not attempt to collect the overdue balance.
    * `expired` - Indicates a subscription that has expired due to running its normal life cycle. Some products may be configured to have an expiration period. An expired subscription then is one that stayed active until it fulfilled its full period.
    * `failed_to_create` - Indicates that signup has failed. (You may see this state in a signup_failure webhook.)
    * `on_hold` - Indicates that a subscription’s billing has been temporarily stopped. While it is expected that the subscription will resume and return to active status, this is still treated as an “End of Life” state because the customer is not paying for services during this time.
    * `suspended` - Indicates that a prepaid subscription has used up all their prepayment balance. If a prepayment is applied, it will return to an active state.
    * `trial_ended` - A subscription in a trial_ended state is a subscription that completed a no-obligation trial and did not have a card on file at the expiration of the trial period. See [Product Pricing – No Obligation Trials](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/plans/creating-plans) for more details.

See [Subscription States](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/management/subscription-states/understand-subscription-states) for more info about subscription states and state transitions.

segments.description:
Per-segment rates for an event-based component. Each entry sets the pricing scheme and prices for one segment, identified by its property values.

Accepted by Create Subscription and Update Subscription, which save the segment rates. Preview Subscription and the signup proforma invoice endpoints validate segments the same way but do not save them. Other endpoints that accept a component `custom_price` reject a `segments` key with a 422 response.

SubscriptionComponentCustomPrice.description:
Create or update custom pricing unique to the subscription, used in place of `price_point_id`. Accepts every attribute of a component custom price, plus `segments` for setting per-segment rates on an event-based component.

Segment-level custom pricing requires a site on Maxio Metering and an event-based component whose meter has segmenting properties. The override takes effect as soon as the request succeeds and prices all of the current billing period's usage at the new rates, including usage recorded before the request. There is no option to schedule the change for a later date.

To read the segment rates back, take the `price_point_id` of the subscription's component (for example, from [Read Subscription Component]($e/Subscription%20Components/readSubscriptionComponent)) and call `GET /components/{component_id}/price_points/{price_point_id}/segments.json`.

SubscriptionComponentCustomPriceSegment.description:
Custom rates for one segment of an event-based component, set on the subscription through `custom_price.segments`.

Identify the segment by the property values that occur in your events, in the same positions as the segmenting properties defined on the component's meter. Each segment in a request must have a unique combination of property values.

SubscriptionState.title: SubscriptionState
SubscriptionState.description:
The state of a subscription.
* **Live States**
    * `active` - A normal, active subscription. It is not in a trial and is paid and up to date.
    * `assessing` - An internal (transient) state that indicates a subscription is in the middle of periodic assessment. Do not base any access decisions in your app on this state, as it may not always be exposed.
    * `pending` - An internal (transient) state that indicates a subscription is in the creation process. Do not base any access decisions in your app on this state, as it may not always be exposed.
    * `trialing` - A subscription in trialing state has a valid trial subscription. This type of subscription may transition to active once payment is received when the trial has ended. Otherwise, it may go to a Problem or End of Life state.
    * `paused` - An internal state that indicates that your account with Advanced Billing is in arrears.
* **Problem States**
    * `past_due` - Indicates that the most recent payment has failed, and payment is past due for this subscription. If you have enabled our automated dunning, this subscription will be in the dunning process (additional status and callbacks from the dunning process will be available in the future). If you are handling dunning and payment updates yourself, you will want to use this state to initiate a payment update from your customers.
    * `soft_failure` - Indicates that normal assessment/processing of the subscription has failed for a reason that cannot be fixed by the Customer. For example, a Soft Fail may result from a timeout at the gateway or incorrect credentials on your part. The subscriptions should be retried automatically. An interface is being built for you to review problems resulting from these events to take manual action when needed.
    * `unpaid` - Indicates an unpaid subscription. A subscription is marked unpaid if the retry period expires and you have configured your [Dunning](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/dunning/overview/understanding-how-dunning-works) settings to have a Final Action of `mark the subscription unpaid`.
* **End of Life States**
    * `canceled` - Indicates a canceled subscription. This may happen at your request (via the API or the web interface) or due to the expiration of the [Dunning](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/dunning/overview/understanding-how-dunning-works) process without payment. See the [Reactivation](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/management/state-management/understand-reactivation-and-resume-scenarios) documentation for info on how to restart a canceled subscription.
    While a subscription is canceled, its period will not advance, it will not accrue any new charges, and Advanced Billing will not attempt to collect the overdue balance.
    * `expired` - Indicates a subscription that has expired due to running its normal life cycle. Some products may be configured to have an expiration period. An expired subscription then is one that stayed active until it fulfilled its full period.
    * `failed_to_create` - Indicates that signup has failed. (You may see this state in a signup_failure webhook.)
    * `on_hold` - Indicates that a subscription’s billing has been temporarily stopped. While it is expected that the subscription will resume and return to active status, this is still treated as an “End of Life” state because the customer is not paying for services during this time.
    * `suspended` - Indicates that a prepaid subscription has used up all their prepayment balance. If a prepayment is applied, it will return to an active state.
    * `trial_ended` - A subscription in a trial_ended state is a subscription that completed a no-obligation trial and did not have a card on file at the expiration of the trial period. See [Product Pricing – No Obligation Trials](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/plans/creating-plans) for more details.

See [Subscription States](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/management/subscription-states/understand-subscription-states) for more info about subscription states and state transitions.

In the Awaiting Signup state, a subscription behaves like any other. It can be canceled, allocated to, or have its billing date changed, etc. When the `initial_billing_at` date hits, the subscription will transition to the expected state. If the product has a trial, the subscription will enter a trial, otherwise it will go active. Setup fees will be respected either before or after the trial, as configured on the price point. If the payment is due at the initial_billing_at and it fails the subscription will be immediately canceled. You can omit the initial_billing_at date to activate the subscription immediately. See the [subscription import](https://docs.maxio.com/configuration/importing/import-subscriptions-from-a-csv#date-format) documentation for more information about Date/Time formats.

The subscription moves to the awaiting signup with a scheduled initial billing date. You can omit the initial_billing_at date to activate the subscription immediately. id.description: The Advanced Billing id of the wallet.

allOf.description: The polymorphic owner type. `subscription` is the only value currently supported.

owner_id.description: The id of the owning subscription.

name.description: (Optional) A merchant-facing label for the wallet, set on create and changeable with [Update Wallet]($e/Wallets/updateWallet). Surrounding spaces are stripped; a blank value is stored as `null`.

wallet_product_id.description: The id of the [Wallet Product]($e/Wallet%20Products/createWalletProduct) that denominates the wallet. Immutable for the life of the wallet.

wallet_product_name.description: The name of the Wallet Product that denominates the wallet.

unit.description: The billing product's unit name, immutable for the life of the wallet.

price_point_id.description: The price point that priced this wallet's [purchases]($e/Wallet%20Purchases/createWalletPurchase), set on create and immutable afterward. Defaults to the Wallet Product's default price point; `null` if the Wallet Product has none and none was given on create.

balance.description: What the wallet can spend now, encoded as a decimal string to avoid floating-point precision loss. This is the number to enforce against. For a metered wallet, it includes usage not yet posted to the ledger, through `metered_through_at`, but only in the response from [Read Wallet]($e/Wallets/readWallet); every other response (list, create, update, archive) reports the balance as of the last ledger write, equal to `posted_balance`, even for a metered wallet. The grants' `remaining` follow this figure, so they add up to it whenever it is zero or more.

posted_balance.description: The balance from written ledger entries alone: grants funded, minus debits written to the ledger, as a decimal string. Always present, also for a wallet with no meter. It equals `balance` wherever no live metered balance is computed: list, create, update, and archive responses, an unlinked or archived wallet, and a read where `metered_stale` is `true`. Only an active, metered wallet read through [Read Wallet]($e/Wallets/readWallet), with `metered_stale` not `true`, can have a `balance` below its `posted_balance`. It stays exact when `metered_stale` is `true`. Reconcile the transactions list (`balance_after`) against this figure, not against `balance`.

allOf.description: The metering meter this wallet is paired with, or `null` for a wallet with no meter. Set on create and immutable afterward.

metered_through_at.description: The point up to which live meter usage has been factored into `balance`. Populated only in the response from [Read Wallet]($e/Wallets/readWallet), for an active, metered wallet on a site with metered consumption enabled; `null` everywhere else, including list, create, update, and archive responses for the same wallet.

metered_recheck_after_seconds.description: How many seconds to wait before re-reading `balance` to see usage past `metered_through_at`. Same availability as `metered_through_at`.

metered_stale.description: `true` when live usage could not be read fresh and `balance` reflects an earlier snapshot. Same availability as `metered_through_at`.

depletion_policy.description: What happens when a debit would take the wallet below zero. Known values: `hard_stop` (the only value you can set today). More values are expected over time, so treat this as an open string and don't fail on one you don't recognize. At the zero boundary, `hard_stop` behaves as set by `hard_stop_overflow`.

allOf.description: Behavior at the hard-stop boundary. `discard` drains the wallet to zero and rejects the excess (the default). `allow_negative` deducts the full amount, letting the balance go negative. The excess past the wallet's grants is booked as an overdraft ledger row with `grant_id` set to `null`.

How the wallet came to exist. `manual` for a wallet created directly with [Create Wallet]($e/Wallets/createWallet). `feature` for a wallet auto-provisioned because a subscription resolved a usage-limit entitlement whose Feature has `wallet_behavior` configured.

feature_key.description: The key of the Feature this wallet was provisioned for, when `origin` is `feature`. `null` for a `manual` wallet.

grants.description: Every grant on the wallet, including ones already spent or expired, in drain order (the order debits would consume the still-open ones in): the soonest-expiring grant first, evergreen grants last.

recurring_funding.description: The wallet's automatic funding schedules, if any. Empty for a `manual` wallet with no funding entitlement. A wallet funds automatically when it's provisioned from a Feature with `wallet_behavior` configured; see [the Wallets concept guide](page:introduction/basic-concepts/wallets#provisioning-a-wallet-from-a-feature).

Wallet.description: A balance, denominated in the unit of a Wallet Product, owned by a subscription. Grants and recurring funding schedules are embedded so a single read shows the full balance breakdown.

errors.description: Human-readable messages. These may be reworded, so match on `code` instead.

Failures that come from record validation, such as a field that fails a model rule, report `validation_failed`.

invoice_number.description: Returned alongside `invoice_uid`: the number of the invoice the purchase created.

WalletErrorResponse1.description: The JSON error body returned by every wallet, transaction, adjustment, purchase, and Wallet Product endpoint for `400`, `404`, `409`, `422`, `500`, and `503` responses. A `403` is not JSON; it is the plain text `403 Forbidden`.

WalletGrant.title: WalletGrant

id.description: The Advanced Billing id of the grant.

name.description: The memo the grant was created with, or `Grant

original.description: The amount the grant was created with, encoded as a decimal string. Never changes after creation.

remaining.description: What the grant can still spend, encoded as a decimal string. On [Read Wallet]($e/Wallets/readWallet) for a metered wallet whose `balance` is the live figure, this is `posted_remaining` less the pending usage drawn from this grant in drain order: usage past a grant spills to the next one, and usage past every grant is an overdraft that belongs to no grant. It never goes below zero, and the grants' `remaining` add up to the wallet's `balance` whenever `balance` is zero or more. Everywhere else it equals `posted_remaining`.

posted_remaining.description: The grant's remainder from written ledger entries alone, encoded as a decimal string. Always present. This is the figure an adjustment checks `expected_remaining` and its bounds against, so send it back, not `remaining`, when correcting a grant.

expires_at.description: When this grant's unconsumed remainder is automatically written off. `null` for an evergreen grant.

expires_on.description: The calendar day `expires_at` falls on, already resolved in the site's time zone.

expired_at.description: When the expiry sweep actually wrote this grant's remainder off. Usually falls shortly after `expires_at`; use `expires_on` for the date the grant expired, not this field. `null` if the grant was never written off (including a grant simply spent to zero before its `expires_at`).

expired_on.description: The calendar day `expired_at` falls on, resolved in the site's time zone.

allOf.description: How the grant was created. `recurring` comes from the wallet's automatic funding schedule (see the wallet's `recurring_funding` array). `manual` comes from a one-time grant posted to [Create Wallet Transaction]($e/Wallet%20Transactions/createWalletTransaction). `initial_balance` comes from a non-zero `initial_balance` at wallet creation. `allowance_increase` comes from raising a funding entitlement's allowance while it's already funding a wallet. `purchase` comes from [Create Wallet Purchase]($e/Wallet%20Purchases/createWalletPurchase).

granted_for_period_start.description: For a `recurring` grant, the start of the funding cadence period this grant covers. `null` for every other origin. After a gap in funding (see `skipped_periods`), this is the period currently in progress, not the oldest period that was missed.

invoice_uid.description: The uid of the invoice that paid for this grant, for a grant with `origin` of `purchase`. `null` for every other origin.

WalletGrant.description: A funding tranche embedded on the wallet. `original` is the amount the grant was created with; `posted_remaining` is what debits and adjustments written to the ledger have left; `remaining` is what can still be spent. Debits drain grants earliest-expiration-first (grants with no expiration are drained last).

WalletHardStopOverflow.title: WalletHardStopOverflow
WalletHardStopOverflow.description: Behavior at the hard-stop boundary. `discard` drains the wallet to zero and rejects the excess (the default). `allow_negative` deducts the full amount, letting the balance go negative. The excess past the wallet's grants is booked as an overdraft ledger row with `grant_id` set to `null`.

product_family_name.description: The name of the Product Family to which the Component belongs. `null` for a Wallet Product, which has no Product Family.

product_family_handle.description: The handle of the Product Family to which the Component belongs. `null` for a Wallet Product, which has no Product Family.

allOf.description: A handle for the component type

overage_prices.description: Applicable only to prepaid usage components. An array of overage price brackets.

price_point_count.description: Count for the number of price points associated with the component

price_points_url.description: URL that points to the location to read the existing price points via GET request

tax_code.description: A string representing the tax code related to the component type. This is especially important when using AvaTax to tax based on locale. This attribute has a max length of 25 characters.

allOf.description: The type of credit to be created when upgrading/downgrading. Defaults to the component and then site setting if one is not provided.
The type of credit to be created when upgrading/downgrading. Defaults to the component and then site setting if one is not provided.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when this component was created

updated_at.description: Timestamp indicating when this component was updated

archived_at.description: Timestamp indicating when this component was archived

hide_date_range_on_invoice.description: (Only available on Relationship Invoicing sites) Boolean flag describing if the service date range should show for the component on generated invoices.

allOf.description: One of the following: Business Software, Consumer Software, Digital Services, Physical Goods, Other

accounting_code.description: E.g. Internal ID or SKU Number

event_based_billing_metric_id.description: (Only for Event Based Components) This is an ID of a metric attached to the component. This metric is used to bill upon collected events.

interval.description: The numerical interval. e.g., an interval of ‘30’ coupled with an interval_unit of day would mean this component’s default price point would renew every 30 days. This property is only available for sites with Multifrequency enabled.

unspsc_code.description: (Optional) Custom UNSPSC commodity code for Level 3/CEDP payment data. When set, this value is sent as the commodity code on invoice line items for this component instead of the default derived from item_category.

features.description: The active feature catalog items attached to this component. Present only when the request includes `include_features=true`.

allOf.description: A rollup of what's using this Wallet Product, for the catalog listing.
A summary of the Wallet Product's default price point, for rendering a catalog listing without a separate price points call.

name.description: The price point's name. Required. Omitting it fails validation with a message that reads `Name: cannot be blank.`, not naming the price point.

entry_price.description: The unit price of the default price point's first bracket, as a decimal string. `null` if there are no brackets.

wallet_configurations.description: Number of wallet templates billing through this product, whether or not any wallet has been created from them yet.

active_wallets.description: Number of active (non-archived) wallets currently denominated by this product.

WalletProductUsageCount.description: A rollup of what's using this Wallet Product, for the catalog listing.
