WalletProductUsageTemplate.title: WalletProductUsageTemplate

plan_name.description: The name of the product or component the Feature is assigned to. `null` when the wallet template has no assigning Feature.

wallet_template_name.description: The label set in `wallet_behavior.name` on the Feature, or the standalone wallet's own `name`.

purchase_mechanism.description: A best-effort label for how this wallet is expected to be replenished. Currently reports `"Overage"` when the wallet template allows a negative balance, and `null` otherwise; there's no persisted field yet distinguishing, for example, an intended "Auto top-up" from "Purchase more" setup. Treat this as informational, not a stable enum.

active.description: `false` when the assigning Feature is archived.

price_point_override.description: `true` when this wallet template is priced at a price point other than the Wallet Product's default.

WalletProductUsageTemplate.description: One wallet template billing through this Wallet Product, joined to the Feature and plan/component that assigns it, when there is one.

total_count.description: Total number of Wallet Products matching the filters, across all pages.

archived_count.description: Not a simple count of archived products matching the filters. With `status=archived`, equals `total_count` (there's nothing else to report). With any other `status`, it's `0` whenever `total_count` is non-zero, and only when `total_count` is `0` does it become the number of archived Wallet Products matching the same `q` search term (ignoring `status`): an empty-state hint, not a running total.

id.description: The id of the grant this purchase created. When the wallet was overdrawn by at least the purchased quantity, the units repay the debt and the grant is still created, with `remaining` of `0` and `original` equal to the purchased quantity.

price_point_id.description: The price point the purchase was priced at.

invoice_uid.description: The uid of the invoice created to collect payment for this purchase.

quantity.description: The number of units purchased, as a decimal string.

expires_at.description: When the purchased units expire, following the funding entitlement's grant expiration policy. `null` when the wallet has no funding entitlement or its entitlements disagree on an expiration policy.

WalletPurchasePreview.title: WalletPurchasePreview

currency.description: The three-letter currency code the `amount` is denominated in, matching the subscription's currency.

quantity.description: The number of units the quote is for, as a decimal string.

amount.description: The price for `quantity` units at this price point, as a decimal string.

WalletPurchasePreview.description: A price quote for a purchase, without charging anything.

balance.description: The wallet's new balance, as a decimal string.

WalletRecurringFunding.title: WalletRecurringFunding

id.description: The Advanced Billing id of the recurring funding schedule.

entitlement_id.description: The usage-limit entitlement this schedule reads its allowance and cadence from.

allowance.description: The entitlement's current allowance, read fresh at request time rather than stored on the wallet. Editing the entitlement changes this immediately, with no separate sync step. `"0"` means the entitlement is configured to grant nothing, a valid, working configuration and not an error. `null` when `status` is `stopped`, since there is no longer an entitlement to read.

next_grant_at.description: When the next automatic grant is due. Grants are applied by a background process shortly after this moment passes, not exactly on it, so a wallet read taken in that window still shows the pre-grant balance. `null` when `status` is `stopped`, and also `null` once the owning subscription has terminated, even while `status` is still `active`: at its next due moment the schedule is stopped with reason `subscription_terminated`.

next_grant_on.description: The calendar day `next_grant_at` falls on, resolved in the site's time zone. `null` under the same conditions as `next_grant_at`.

skipped_periods.description: Cumulative count of due moments that passed without a grant being made (for example, during an outage). A gap in funding is visible here without cross-referencing the ledger.

allOf.description: `active`: refilling normally. `erroring`: the schedule is still due and retrying, but the last attempt couldn't be written (see `reason`); correcting the underlying entitlement resumes funding on the next run with no action needed on the wallet itself. `stopped`: funding has ended for good (see `reason`); units already granted stay on the wallet and remain spendable, but no further automatic grants will be made.

Set whenever `status` isn't `active`. Accompanying `stopped`: `entitlement_missing` (an ordinary product or component change removed the entitlement), `wallet_archived` (the wallet was archived), `subscription_terminated` (the subscription reached a terminal state; funding resumes if the subscription returns to a granting state, for example on reactivation, without back-granting the periods it missed), `feature_removed` (the subscription no longer has this Feature), `wallet_behavior_disabled` (the Feature no longer has `wallet_behavior` configured), `superseded_by_replacement` (a later entitlement now funds this wallet instead), or `subscription_prepaid` (the subscription switched to prepaid, which cannot carry an active wallet). Accompanying `erroring`: `allowance_not_representable` (the entitlement's current allowance doesn't fit the wallet's amount encoding) or `balance_at_capacity` (granting it would push the balance past the maximum supported value).

WalletRecurringFunding.description: Describes automatic funding of the wallet from a usage-limit entitlement. Set up by configuring `wallet_behavior` on the Feature behind that entitlement, not by any parameter on the wallet itself. This field is an array as of its first release. The array currently holds zero or one element, and is expected to hold several once a wallet can be funded by more than one entitlement.

WalletRecurringFundingStatus.title: WalletRecurringFundingStatus
WalletRecurringFundingStatus.description: `active`: refilling normally. `erroring`: the schedule is still due and retrying, but the last attempt couldn't be written (see `reason`); correcting the underlying entitlement resumes funding on the next run with no action needed on the wallet itself. `stopped`: funding has ended for good (see `reason`); units already granted stay on the wallet and remain spendable, but no further automatic grants will be made.

allOf.description: A balance, denominated in the unit of a Wallet Product, owned by a subscription. Grants and recurring funding schedules are embedded so a single read shows the full balance breakdown.

WalletTransaction.title: WalletTransaction

id.description: The Advanced Billing id of the ledger row.

kind.description: The kind of ledger row. Known values: `grant`, `debit`, `adjustment`, `initial_balance`, and `expiration`. More kinds are expected over time, so treat this as an open string and don't fail on one you don't recognize. Only `grant` and `debit` are accepted on [Create Wallet Transaction]($e/Wallet%20Transactions/createWalletTransaction). `adjustment` rows are written by [Create Wallet Adjustment]($e/Wallet%20Adjustments/createWalletAdjustment), `initial_balance` rows only by a seeded [Create Wallet]($e/Wallets/createWallet), and `expiration` rows only by the automatic expiry sweep that writes off an unconsumed grant once its `expires_at` passes.

amount.description: A decimal string, **signed** on this resource. Non-negative for grants, negative for debits and expirations, either sign for adjustments. A grant row written after an overdraft repayment carries only what was left after the repayment (possibly `"0.0"`), not the grant's `original`.

grant_id.description: The grant this row is attributed to. `null` for an overdraft row (a `kind: debit` row draining the below-zero portion of a balance, attributed to no grant), for an overdraft-repayment row (the `kind: grant` row that pays an existing negative balance back to zero, written before any remainder becomes a new grant), and for an overdraft correction (a `kind: adjustment` row posted against an overdraft entry, which credits no grant).

source_transaction_id.description: For an `adjustment` row posted against a specific usage entry, the id of the `debit` row it corrects. `null` for every other kind, and for adjustments made against a grant's balance directly.

source_corrections_total.description: For a `debit` row only, the signed sum (as a decimal string) of every adjustment posted against it so far (`"0.0"` when none). `null` for every other kind. The row's own `amount` is never rewritten, so a caller deriving the entry's corrected quantity nets this out of `amount`, and sends this value back as `expected_source_corrections` on a further correction.

balance_after.description: The wallet's posted balance immediately after this row was applied, as a decimal string. Compare it with the wallet's `posted_balance`, not its `balance`.

metered_from_at.description: For a row that closed a metered usage window (an hourly close, a depletion, or an expiry write-off), the start of that window. `null` on every other row.

metered_through_at.description: The end of the usage window this row closed. `null` on every other row.

conversion_rate_applied.description: The meter-to-wallet-unit conversion rate applied to compute this row's `amount`, as a decimal string. `null` on every other row.

invoice_uid.description: The uid of the invoice behind a purchase's rows: the grant-creating row and, when the purchase repaid an overdraft, the repayment row. `null` on every other row.

memo.description: Free-text note. For an `adjustment` row, carries the required `reason`.

WalletTransaction.description: One append-only row on the wallet's ledger. Always appears bare inside a `wallet_transactions` array, never wrapped in its own key.

WalletTransactionResultResponse.title: WalletTransactionResultResponse

requested_amount.description: `kind: debit` only. The amount that was requested, as a decimal string.

drained_amount.description: `kind: debit` only. The amount actually drained from the wallet's grants, as a decimal string.

rejected_amount.description: `kind: debit` only, as a decimal string. Under `hard_stop_overflow: discard`, this is the requested amount minus what the wallet could cover (`"0.0"` on a full drain). Always `"0.0"` under `allow_negative`; nothing is rejected, and the balance goes negative instead.

balance.description: The wallet's new balance, as a decimal string.

WalletTransactionResultResponse.description: Returned by [Create Wallet Transaction]($e/Wallet%20Transactions/createWalletTransaction). `wallet_transactions` and `balance` are always present. `requested_amount`, `drained_amount`, and `rejected_amount` are present only when the request's `kind` was `debit`.

subscription_id.description: The subscription that will own the wallet.

wallet_product_id.description: The [Wallet Product]($e/Wallet%20Products/createWalletProduct) that will denominate the wallet: its numeric id, or its handle prefixed with `handle:` (for example `handle:token-pack`). A bare handle with no prefix is looked up as an id and returns `404`. Immutable once the wallet is created.

name.description: (Optional) A merchant-facing label for the wallet. Surrounding spaces are stripped; a blank value is stored as `null`.

depletion_policy.description: Defaults to `hard_stop`, currently the only supported value.

allOf.description: Defaults to `discard`.

meter_id.description: Pairs the wallet with a merchant-owned metering meter, so its balance factors in live usage (see the wallet resource's `meter` and `metered_through_at` fields). Only a `sum` or `count` meter can be paired. Requires metered wallet consumption to be enabled for the site, checked whenever this or `conversion_rate` is sent: `403` (plain text, not JSON) if it isn't. A meter id that doesn't resolve to a merchant-owned meter on this site, including a system-maintained shadow meter, is `404`. Immutable once the wallet is created.

conversion_rate.description: How many wallet units one meter unit is worth, as a decimal string with at most 8 fractional digits, greater than `0` and below 10^16. Send fractional values as strings: a JSON number with a decimal point is rejected with `422`, because a double-precision float may already have lost precision before the request arrives. Only meaningful with `meter_id`. Defaults to `"1.0"`. Immutable once the wallet is created.

price_point_id.description: The price point used to price [Create Wallet Purchase]($e/Wallet%20Purchases/createWalletPurchase) calls against this wallet. Must belong to the Wallet Product, and can't be archived or a subscription-specific custom price point. Defaults to the Wallet Product's default price point. Immutable once the wallet is created.

initial_balance.description: (Optional) A free opening balance, not a purchase and not reflected on any invoice. When non-zero, wallet creation also writes an initial-balance grant and a matching `initial_balance` ledger row. Omitted or exactly `0` creates a zero-balance wallet, not an error. Encoded as a decimal string with at most 8 fractional digits, and must be non-negative and below 10^16. Send fractional values as strings: a JSON number with a decimal point is rejected with `422`, because a double-precision float may already have lost precision before the request arrives.

initial_balance_expires_at.description: An expiration for the initial-balance grant. Only accepted together with a non-zero `initial_balance`, and must be in the future. Accepts either a bare calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), resolved to the end of that day in the site's time zone, or a full timestamp. A calendar day that doesn't exist, such as `2027-02-30`, is rejected with `422` rather than rolled into the next month.

name.description: A merchant-facing label for the wallet. Surrounding spaces are stripped; a blank or `null` value clears it.

unit_name.description: The name of the unit the Wallet Product's usage is measured in, for example `tokens`.

allOf.description: One of the following: Business Software, Consumer Software, Digital Services, Physical Goods, Other
Creates one price point for the Wallet Product in the same call. Ignored if `price_points` is also sent.

price_points.description: Creates several price points for the Wallet Product in the same call, winning over `price_point` if both are sent. The first price point created becomes the Wallet Product's default. The whole call is one transaction: if any price point in the array fails validation, nothing is created, including the Wallet Product itself.

allOf.description: One of the following: Business Software, Consumer Software, Digital Services, Physical Goods, Other
Determines the direction of the movement. The amount itself is always sent positive.

amount.description: Always positive; `kind` determines the sign written to the ledger. Encoded as a decimal string with at most 8 fractional digits. Send fractional values as strings: a JSON number with a decimal point is rejected with `422`, because a double-precision float may already have lost precision before the request arrives.

expires_at.description: An expiration for the grant this creates. Only accepted with `kind: grant`; sending it with `kind: debit` is rejected. Omit it for an evergreen grant. Accepts either a bare calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), resolved to the end of that day in the site's time zone, or a full timestamp. A calendar day that doesn't exist, such as `2027-02-30`, is rejected with `422` rather than rolled into the next month.

event.description: A string describing which event type produced the given webhook

id.description: The unique identifier for the webhook (unique across all of Chargify). This is not changed on a retry/replay of the same webhook, so it may be used to avoid duplicate action for the same event.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the webhook was created

last_error.description: Text describing the status code and/or error from the last failed attempt to send the Webhook. When a webhook is retried and accepted, this field will be cleared.

last_error_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the last non-acceptance occurred. If a webhook is later resent and accepted, this field will be cleared.

accepted_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the webhook was accepted by the merchant endpoint. When a webhook is explicitly replayed by the merchant, this value will be cleared until it is accepted again.

last_sent_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the most recent attempt was made to send the webhook

last_sent_url.description: The url that the endpoint was last sent to.

successful.description: “A boolean flag describing whether the webhook was accepted by the webhook endpoint for the most recent attempt. (Acceptance is defined by receiving a “200 OK” HTTP response within a reasonable timeframe, e.g., 15 seconds.)”

body.description: The data sent within the webhook post

InvoiceEventPayment.description: A nested data structure detailing the method of payment

BasicAuth.description: The `username` is a Maxio Chargify API key. The `password` is `x`.

tags.name: API Exports
tags.description: API Exports allow you to generate and download bulk exports of subscriptions, invoices, and proforma invoices as asynchronous batch jobs, useful for reporting or migrating data outside the standard paginated list endpoints. For more information, see [Billing Export Fields Reference](https://docs.maxio.com/insights/data-export/field-references/billing-export-fields-reference#invoice-line-items-fields).

tags.name: Advance Invoice
tags.description: Use the Advance Invoice feature to issue, retrieve, or void an invoice for a subscription ahead of its normal billing schedule, collecting an outstanding balance before the next scheduled renewal. For more information, see [Issue Advance Invoices for Subscription Renewals](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/invoicing/advance-invoices/issue-advance-invoices-for-subscription-renewals).

tags.name: Billing Portal
tags.description: The Billing Portal object allows you to enable, disable, and manage customer access to the self-service Billing Portal, where customers can view invoices and manage their own payment details. For more information, see [Understand the Billing Portal](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/billing-portal/overview/understand-the-billing-portal).

tags.name: Coupons
tags.description:
The Coupon object defines a discount, either a percentage or a fixed amount, that can be applied to a subscription to reduce the subscription's billing amount.

Coupons can be restricted to a specific Product Family, limited to a date range, and configured to apply once or recur over a set duration. For more information, see [Understand Coupons](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/coupons/understand-coupons).

tags.name: Component Features
tags.description:
The Component Feature object attaches a Feature Template to a Component as a feature catalog item with a concrete value, granting that feature to subscribers through the component.

A component feature applies to the whole component by default, or can be scoped to a single component price point as an override. For more information, see [Configure Entitlements](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/entitlements/configure-entitlements).

tags.name: Components
tags.description:
The Component object represents an add-on item, such as a metered usage charge, quantity-based feature, or on/off toggle, that can be added to a subscription alongside the subscription's base Product. With the new catalog experience, the UI labels components as Products, while the API keeps the component name. See [Catalog terminology](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/overview/using-the-new-product-catalog#catalog-terminology).

Components belong to a Product Family and are billed according to their pricing scheme and kind. Components can also grant features to subscribers through [Create Component Feature Catalog Item]($e/Component%20Features/createComponentFeature). For more information, see [Understand Products](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/products/understand-products) and [Hybrid pricing](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/products/use-product-pricing-schemes#hybrid-pricing).

tags.name: Component: Price Points
tags.description:
The Component Price Point object defines a specific pricing configuration for a Component, including the price point's rate structure and billing interval.

A single Component can have multiple price points, allowing different subscriptions to be billed for the same component under different terms.

tags.name: Customers
tags.description:
The Customer object represents the person or organization being billed and is the anchor that subscriptions, payment profiles, and invoices are all attached to.

A customer record stores contact and billing details (name, address, tax exemption status, locale) along with references to related records, such as the customer's default subscription group. For more information, see [Understand Customers for Subscription Management](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/customers/understand-customers-for-subscription-management).

tags.name: Custom Fields
tags.description: Custom Fields let you define Metafields for a resource type and manage the Metadata values attached to individual records, so you can capture and store additional data beyond built-in system fields. For more information, see [Understand Custom Fields](https://docs.maxio.com/configuration/advanced-billing/custom-fields/understand-custom-fields).

tags.name: Entitlements
tags.description:
Entitlements report what a subscription is allowed to do, and how much of it, based on the features granted by the subscription's products and components.

When more than one product or component grants the same feature, the values are aggregated into one entry per feature key and periodicity. For more information, see [Read Subscription Entitlements with the API](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/entitlements/read-subscription-entitlements-with-the-api).

tags.name: Events
tags.description:
The Event object records a discrete occurrence within your account, such as a payment, renewal, or subscription state change.

The key identifies which type of event occurred, and event_specific_data carries a payload whose shape depends on that key.

tags.name: Events-Based Billing: Segments
tags.description:
The Segment object defines a distinct pricing variation within an event-based billing metric, based on one or more property values, such as a specific country or usage category.

Each segment carries its own set of prices, letting a single metric charge different rates depending on which segment an event falls into.

tags.name: Feature Templates
tags.description:
The Feature Template object defines a feature once at the site level, such as Single Sign-On, a monthly API call limit, or a support tier.

A feature template is not billable on its own. Attach the template to products or components to grant the feature to subscribers. The kind (access_right, usage_limit, or service_right) determines how the feature's value behaves. For more information, see [Configure Entitlements](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/entitlements/configure-entitlements).

tags.name: Insights
tags.description: The Insights endpoints provide aggregate site-level statistics, such as customer and subscription counts, giving a high-level snapshot of account activity.

tags.name: Invoices
tags.description:
The Invoice object is the billing document generated for a subscription, itemizing charges, taxes, and payments, and tracking amounts owed.

The role indicates what triggered the invoice (signup, renewal, usage, proration, etc.), and the status and due_date reflect where an invoice stands in the payment lifecycle. For more information, see [Get Started with Invoicing](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/invoicing/overview/get-started-with-invoicing).

tags.name: Offers
tags.description:
The Offer object packages a combination of products, components, and coupons into a single option that customers can subscribe to, just like a product. Once an offer is defined, the offer can be used as an alternative to a product when creating subscriptions.

Offers are commonly used to power self-service signup pages without requiring each pricing combination to be built manually. For more information, see [Understand Offers](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/offers/understand-offers).

tags.name: Payment Profiles
tags.description: The Payment Profile object represents a stored payment method on a customer's account. For more information, see [Managing Payment Methods](https://docs.maxio.com/getting-started/maxio-platform-basics/advanced-billing-overview-and-resources/subscription-summary-tabs/managing-payment-methods).

tags.name: Product Families
tags.description: The Product Family object groups related Products, components, and coupons together for organizational purposes, such as products belonging to a single line of business, each sharing a family-level handle and accounting code. For more information, see [Organize Product Families](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/plans/organize-product-families).

tags.name: Product Features
tags.description:
The Product Feature object attaches a Feature Template to a Product as a feature catalog item with a concrete value, granting that feature to subscribers through the product.

A product feature applies to the whole product by default, or can be scoped to a single product price point as an override. For more information, see [Configure Entitlements](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/entitlements/configure-entitlements).

tags.name: Products
tags.description:
The Product object defines what you sell, including default pricing, billing interval, and trial configuration. With the new catalog experience, the UI labels products as Plans, while the API keeps the product name. See [Catalog terminology](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/overview/using-the-new-product-catalog#catalog-terminology).

Products are grouped under a Product Family and are the base type a customer subscribes to. Products can also grant features to subscribers through [Create Product Feature Catalog Item]($e/Product%20Features/createProductFeature). For more information, see [Understand Plans](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/plans/understand-plans).

tags.name: Product: Price Points
tags.description:
The Product Price Point object defines a specific pricing configuration for a Product, including price, billing interval, and trial terms.

A single Product can have multiple price points, letting you offer different rates or terms for the same product without creating separate products. Custom price points (type `custom`) can't be updated, set as the product's default, or given currency prices. Currency prices must mirror the price point's primary pricing, so if the price point defines a trial or setup fee, each currency must define one too. For more information, see [Setting Up Plan Price Points](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/plans/setting-up-plan-price-points).

tags.name: Proforma Invoices
tags.description: The Proforma Invoice object is a preview of an upcoming invoice, showing the charges a customer will be billed before the actual invoice is issued. A proforma invoice is not a finalized billing document and is commonly used to give customers advance visibility into what they owe. For more information, see [Understand Proforma Invoices](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/invoicing/proforma-invoices/understand-proforma-invoices).

tags.name: Reason Codes
tags.description:
The Reason Code object defines a churn reason that can be presented to customers when they cancel a subscription, such as "too expensive" or "switching providers."

Reason codes give merchants visibility into why subscribers are canceling. For more information, see [Configure Churn Reason Codes](https://docs.maxio.com/configuration/advanced-billing/settings/churn-reason-codes).

tags.name: Referral Codes
tags.description: The Referral Code object represents a code attached to a subscription, used to track and validate referrals as part of a referral program. For more information, see [Understand Referrals](https://docs.maxio.com/configuration/advanced-billing/understand-referrals).

tags.name: Sales Commissions
tags.description:
Sales Commissions allow sellers with financial access to retrieve commission data for a site with Advanced Analytics enabled.

These endpoints use a different, user-level authentication method than the rest of the API, since commission data is tied to the seller rather than an individual site.

tags.name: Sites
tags.description: The Site object represents a single billing account and holds site-wide configuration, such as default currency, tax settings, net terms, and which billing features are enabled. For more information, see [Understand Advanced Billing Sites](https://docs.maxio.com/configuration/advanced-billing/sites/sites-overview).

tags.name: Subscriptions
tags.description: Subscriptions connect a customer to a product and drive all recurring billing for that relationship, including invoice generation, billing start dates, and pricing structure across plan-based and planless configurations. For more information, see [Understand Subscriptions](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/overview/understand-subscriptions).

tags.name: Subscription Components
tags.description: Use the Subscription Components object to allocate, adjust, and report usage for the components attached to a subscription, including quantity-based, metered, and event-based components. For more information, see [Managing Components and Usage](https://docs.maxio.com/getting-started/maxio-platform-basics/advanced-billing-overview-and-resources/subscription-summary-tabs/managing-components-and-usage).

tags.name: Subscription Groups
tags.description: The Subscription Group object links multiple subscriptions for a single customer under one shared payment profile and collection method, so you can consolidate billing instead of managing payment details separately for each subscription. For more information, see [Understand Subscription Groups](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/configuration/subscription-groups/understand-subscription-groups).

tags.name: Subscription Group Invoice Account
tags.description: The Subscription Group Invoice Account object lets you manage prepayments and service credits for the shared invoice account of a Subscription Group, applying at the group level rather than to an individual subscription.

tags.name: Subscription Group Status
tags.description: Use the Subscription Group Status object to manage the lifecycle of a Subscription Group as a whole, such as canceling every subscription within the group together.

tags.name: Subscription Invoice Account
tags.description: The Subscription Invoice Account object lets you manage a subscription's account balance, including prepayments, service credits, and refunds. For more information, see [Recording Prepayments](https://docs.maxio.com/getting-started/maxio-platform-basics/advanced-billing-overview-and-resources/subscription-summary-tabs/recording-prepayments) and [Give, Deduct, and Apply Service Credits](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/management/subscription-actions/give-deduct-and-apply-service-credits).

tags.name: Subscription Notes
tags.description:
The Subscription Note object stores an internal note attached to a subscription, used to record context, decisions, or history for your team.

Notes are never exposed to the customer; they exist purely for internal reference.

tags.name: Subscription Products
tags.description: Use the Subscription Products object to migrate a subscription from one product or price point to another, including previewing the effects of a migration before committing to it. For more information, see [Upgrade or Downgrade a Subscription](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/management/subscription-actions/upgrade-or-downgrade-a-subscription).

tags.name: Subscription Renewals
tags.description: The Subscription Renewals object lets you schedule, preview, and manage a subscription's upcoming renewal, including locking in specific pricing or canceling a scheduled renewal before it takes effect. For more information, see [Understand Scheduled Renewal](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/configuration/term-renewal/scheduled-renewal).

tags.name: Subscription Status
tags.description: Subscription Status allows you to manage a subscription's lifecycle, including retrying a failed payment, canceling, pausing, resuming, and reactivating a subscription. For more information, see [Understand Subscription States](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/subscriptions/management/subscription-states/understand-subscription-states).

tags.name: Wallets
tags.description:
The Wallet object is a balance, owned by a subscription and denominated in the unit of a Wallet Product, that you can create, fund, drain, and read through the API.

Wallets suit prepaid allowances, credits, and consumption pools that don't map cleanly onto the regular usage-billing cycle. Every balance change is recorded on the wallet's append-only ledger. For more information, see [Understand Wallets](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/wallets/understand-wallets).

tags.name: Wallet Transactions
tags.description: Use Wallet Transactions to fund a wallet with a one-time grant, consume units with a direct debit, and read the wallet's append-only ledger. For more information, see [Understand Wallets](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/wallets/understand-wallets).

tags.name: Wallet Adjustments
tags.description: Wallet Adjustments post a signed correction against a specific grant, or against an overdraft, on a wallet's ledger. Adjustments are intended for support and operations corrections, and each adjustment requires a reason that is recorded on the ledger. For more information, see [Understand Wallets](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/wallets/understand-wallets).

tags.name: Wallet Purchases
tags.description: Wallet Purchases let a subscription buy additional prepaid units for a wallet, charged according to the subscription's collection method. A purchase can be previewed to quote the price before anything is charged. For more information, see [Understand Wallets](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/wallets/understand-wallets).

tags.name: Wallet Products
tags.description: The Wallet Product object is a billing product created specifically to denominate wallets and to price wallet purchases. A Wallet Product does not belong to a product family, and the Wallet Product behind a wallet cannot be changed after the wallet is created. For more information, see [Create and Manage Wallet Products](https://docs.maxio.com/billing/catalog/wallets/create-and-manage-wallet-products).

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
The Webhook object represents a single notification sent to your configured endpoint when an event occurs.

A webhook tracks delivery status, including when it was last sent, whether the merchant endpoint accepted it, and any error from a failed attempt. For more information, see [Understand Webhooks in Advanced Billing](https://docs.maxio.com/configuration/advanced-billing/webhooks/understand-webhooks-in-advanced-billing).
